Hearing this, all cried, "Jaya! Jaya!", and the students said: "Vidyasagara, we regard You as our life."
Mahaprabhu duly honoured everyone and set out for home together with the two (Gadadhara and Lokanatha).
What more can I say of Sri Gauranga's departure? Tears flowed from the Lord and all His family.
Meanwhile in Navadvipa Mother Shachi, without Gora, wandered hither and thither like a cow that has lost its calf.
At that time Gaurachandra returned home; seeing Him, Shachi was like one whose life had returned to an empty body.
Gauranga bowed at His mother's feet, and Shachi, embracing Him round the neck, wept uncontrollably.
Gorachand said: "Mother, do not weep, do not weep. I am hungry — go and cook quickly."
Hearing this, Shachi hurried to cook, while Gaura bathed in the Ganga with the devotees and came back.
Having worshipped Vishnu, He offered the food and then joyfully dined with the devotees.
In the afternoon Mahaprabhu wandered about the town and defeated great pandits in debate.
All said: "Nimai Pandita is the crown of scholars. Such a Vidyasagara has never been heard of anywhere."
Little by little the sun of the fame of Gaura the scholar shone forth, and in that same Navadvipa His wedding took place.
Vallabhacharya, like the royal sage Bhishmaka, honoured and respected among noble brahmanas for his family and character —

My Lord calls her Sri Rukmini. Sri Gaurasundara took her as His wife.

Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, came — in intellect like Brihaspati, most skilled in the shastras.

After all, there is a spot visible on the moon, and its colour is a dull silver, secondary."
Hearing this, Nimai Vidyasagara joyfully and affectionately praised Sri Achyutananda and said:
"The comparison of the face (to the moon) lies in its delightfulness. No one thing can be compared (to another) in every respect."
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said: "Now I understand. But another thought has come to my mind:
Madana-Gopala is Krishna, Bhagavan Himself. With whom am I to compare Him?

Hearing the boy's words, Sri Shachinandana, with wonder in His heart, said: "Listen, dear one:

Sri Gauranga asked: "How can I firmly believe that?" Sri Achyuta replied: "A thing is revealed by its power:
the gods who drink nectar, when they drink the nectar of the Name, consider themselves to have fully attained their goal — the shastras are the evidence of this."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu melted with hidden love and, taking Achyuta on His lap, kissed him on the head.

advaita-prakasha.title: Бананы для Гауры: Кришнамишра предлагает их «Гаурайа намах»; Гаура отрыгивает бананами
advaita-prakasha.summary: Сита прячет любимые Гаурангой бананы; маленький Кришнамишра находит их, предлагает Гауре с мантрой «Гаурайа намах» и съедает как прасад; Ачьюта признаётся лишь, что прежде выпил молоко для Гауры, — и след материнского шлепка проявился на теле Гауры; Сита гонится с палкой за Кришнамишрой, Адвайта выслушивает его — «в Гауре заключено имя Кришны»; Гаура же отказывается от еды: кто-то во сне накормил Его бананами, — и отрыгивает их запахом.

verses.text: Послушайте однажды дивное сказание о Сите, матери мира, чья жизнь была отдана Гауре.
Любимое лакомство Гауранги — бананы сорта чампа; чтобы угостить Гауру, она спрятала их.
Мать ушла омываться в Ганге; найдя дом пустым, Кришнамишра стал искать, что бы поесть.
Ища, он нашёл спелые бананы; вечный преданный Кришны, ребёнок рассудил про себя:
«Мать хочет угостить бананами Гауру; если я их съем, это будет оскорблением.
Но если, предложив, съем их как прасад Гауранги, в этом не будет вины».
Сначала произнеся великую мантру пранавы, он предложил их, сказав: «Гаурайа намах».
Считая бананы маха-прасадом, он коснулся ими головы и с радостью съел их.
Мать Сита, омывшись в Ганге, вернулась домой, думая поднести бананы Гауре.
Там, где она спрятала бананы, их не оказалось; подумав, что их съели сыновья, она опечалилась.
Сначала она позвала Шри Ачьютананду и спросила: «Я оставила бананы для Гауры — кто их съел?»
Шри Ачьюта ответил: «Мать, ты всеведуща: ты знаешь моё поведение и мои мысли.
По детскому озорству я выпил молоко, приготовленное для служения Гауре, и после твоего наказания получил урок».
Что я, ничтожный, скажу о величии Ачьюты, чья душа неотлична от Шри Кришны Чайтаньи?
В исступлении Гауры он выпил молоко для служения Гауре, и мать Ачьюты дала ему шлепка —
и след того шлепка появился на теле Гауры! Видя это, все люди изумились.
Вечно совершенные преданные Бхагавана и сама преданность — у этих двух непостижимая сила.
Духовная преданность и духовные преданные неотличны по душе от Кришны — так написано в шастрах.
Затем Сита позвала Кришнадаса Мишру и спросила его: «Кто съел бананы для служения Гауре?»
Кришнамишра ответил: «Мать, что в этом дурного? Я съел их, предложив Гауре».
Услышав это, мать Сита слегка улыбнулась и с палкой в руке побежала за ребёнком.
В страхе Кришнамишра бросился к Адвайте. Увидев Ситу позади, лучший из владык сказал:
«Не бей! Сначала Я выслушаю, как было». Услышав запрет Господа, Сита остановилась.
Господь спросил: «Кришнамишра, в чём ты провинился?» Кришнамишра мягко ответил Ему:
«Мать оставила бананы, чтобы угостить Гауру. Я съел их, предложив Гауре, — вины не знаю».
Господь спросил: «С какой мантрой ты предложил?» Ребёнок ответил: «С пранавой: „Гаурайа намах“».
Господь сказал: «Вместо „Гаурайа“ следовало сказать „Кришнайа“». Ребёнок ответил: «В Гауре заключено имя Кришны».
Господь изумился его словам и, охваченный любовью, расцеловал лицо ребёнка.
Услышав вывод сына, Сита изумилась и подумала: «Благословен, благословен мой сын!»
Затем всех позвали к трапезе. Гаура сказал: «Я уже поел».
Господь спросил: «Когда же Ты поел?» Гаура ответил: «Кто-то, пока Я спал, накормил Меня бананами».
Сказав так, Он отрыгнул — и, почуяв запах бананов, все изумились.
Шри Адвайта подумал: «Кришна подвластен преданным: Он, несомненно, вкусил бананы, поднесённые Кришнамишрой.
Как велика Моя удача, что у Меня такой сын: его деяниями очистится мир».
Едва подумав так, Господь размяк сердцем от любви, и из обоих Его глаз непрестанно лились слёзы.
Услышав эту истину, Сита забылась в любви и подумала: «Удаче моего сына нет предела.
Я поистине счастливица, родившая жемчужину: из моего чрева явился чистый преданный Кришны».

and the mark of that slap appeared on Gaura's body! Seeing this, all the people were amazed.

Then Sita called Krishnadasa Mishra and asked him: "Who has eaten the bananas meant for Gaura's service?"

"Mother kept the bananas to treat Gaura. I ate them after offering them to Gaura — I know of no fault."

The Lord asked: "When did You eat?" Gaura replied: "Someone fed Me bananas while I was asleep."

Hearing this truth, Sita was lost in love and thought: "There is no limit to my son's good fortune.
I am truly fortunate to have borne a jewel: from my womb a pure devotee of Krishna has appeared."

Hearing this, the devotees rejoiced still more and all together began the sankirtana of the Name.
Sri Advaita danced, Haridasa danced, Sri Achyutananda and Krishnadasa danced.
Watching Krishna Mishra dance, Mahaprabhu laughed: Gaura took pains to make the devotees dance.

Thus a year of Gaura's passed, and in that time He studied the Vedas and the Bhagavata.
Seeing this, the pandits were amazed, and the Acharya spoke of Gaura's unearthly qualities.
Inconceivable is the glory of Gadadhara Pandita: the Four-faced One cannot find the limit of his qualities.

Wonderful is the power of association with Sri Gauranga: Lokanatha became a master of the Bhagavata.
Hearing the meaning of the verses, he always shed tears of love, and all said: "Krishna has shown mercy to Lokanatha."
One day Lokanatha said to the Acharya: "Lord, tell me, how is Krishna to be attained?"
The Lord replied: "Receive the mantra of Krishna: it very soon draws Krishna."
Hearing this, Lokanatha rejoiced and received the mantra from my Lord, standing in the waters of the Ganga.
Inconceivable is the power of the king of Vaishnava mantras: as soon as he received it, he obtained pure loving devotion.
Then Lokanatha, clasping the feet of Sri Advaita, wept in the ecstasy of love and humbly offered many praises.
The Lord said: "Do not weep, calm your mind: very soon you will attain Radha and Krishna."
Having said this, the Lord took Lokanatha by the hand and led him to Mahaprabhu.
The Lord said: "Listen carefully, Nimai: teach Lokanatha the search for truth."
Having said this, He entrusted His beloved disciple to Gaura, and Sri Gauranga accepted Lokanatha as His own.
One day Gora said to the Acharya: "Allow Me to leave — I wish to return home."
The Lord said: "To let you go breaks My heart. But you are free both to appear and to disappear."
Having said this, the Lord sank into the ocean of love, and then, restraining His love, said to all:
"This Nimai is extraordinarily learned in all the shastras — I give Him the title Vidyasagara (Ocean of Learning)."
Hearing this, all cried, "Jaya! Jaya!", and the students said: "Vidyasagara, we regard You as our life."
Mahaprabhu duly honoured everyone and set out for home together with the two (Gadadhara and Lokanatha).
What more can I say of Sri Gauranga's departure? Tears flowed from the Lord and all His family.
Meanwhile in Navadvipa Mother Shachi, without Gora, wandered hither and thither like a cow that has lost its calf.
At that time Gaurachandra returned home; seeing Him, Shachi was like one whose life had returned to an empty body.
Gauranga bowed at His mother's feet, and Shachi, embracing Him round the neck, wept uncontrollably.
Gorachand said: "Mother, do not weep, do not weep. I am hungry — go and cook quickly."
Hearing this, Shachi hurried to cook, while Gaura bathed in the Ganga with the devotees and came back.
Having worshipped Vishnu, He offered the food and then joyfully dined with the devotees.
In the afternoon Mahaprabhu wandered about the town and defeated great pandits in debate.
All said: "Nimai Pandita is the crown of scholars. Such a Vidyasagara has never been heard of anywhere."
Little by little the sun of the fame of Gaura the scholar shone forth, and in that same Navadvipa His wedding took place.
Vallabhacharya, like the royal sage Bhishmaka, honoured and respected among noble brahmanas for his family and character —
his daughter was the chaste Lakshmi, the supreme pleasure potency, full of all virtues, exceedingly beautiful.
My Lord calls her Sri Rukmini. Sri Gaurasundara took her as His wife.
Then Gora opened a school and taught students: each student studied whatever shastra he wished.
Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, came — in intellect like Brihaspati, most skilled in the shastras.
Having him, Mahaprabhu rejoiced boundlessly and taught him grammar and poetics.
One day Sri Achyuta asked Gaurachandra: "How can a face be fittingly compared to the moon?
After all, there is a spot visible on the moon, and its colour is a dull silver, secondary."
Hearing this, Nimai Vidyasagara joyfully and affectionately praised Sri Achyutananda and said:
"The comparison of the face (to the moon) lies in its delightfulness. No one thing can be compared (to another) in every respect."
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said: "Now I understand. But another thought has come to my mind:
Madana-Gopala is Krishna, Bhagavan Himself. With whom am I to compare Him?
I find nothing to liken Him to. Tell me a comparison — dispel my doubt."
Hearing the boy's words, Sri Shachinandana, with wonder in His heart, said: "Listen, dear one:
Sri Krishna is being, consciousness and bliss, full of all potencies. He is the standard of comparison, and there is no comparison for Him.
As other tastes are compared to nectar — is there anything in the world with which to compare nectar?"
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said: "You know everything. The nectar of the name of Hari is sweeter than nectar itself."
Sri Gauranga asked: "How can I firmly believe that?" Sri Achyuta replied: "A thing is revealed by its power:
the gods who drink nectar, when they drink the nectar of the Name, consider themselves to have fully attained their goal — the shastras are the evidence of this."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu melted with hidden love and, taking Achyuta on His lap, kissed him on the head.
The most secret pastimes of Sri Chaitanya with His devotees — I have no power to describe even their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

advaita-prakasha.title: Первый рис Гопаладаса: из всех предметов младенец касается стоп Гауранги
advaita-prakasha.summary: На обряде первого риса младенец Гопаладас не трогает разложенных перед ним предметов, а касается стоп Гауранги; Адвайта предсказывает, что он станет венцом праведных, говорит, что стопа брахмана равна стопе Вишну, и намёками раскрывает истину о Гауранге; все пляшут в санкиртане, а Гаура смеётся, глядя на пляску Кришнамишры.

verses.text: Однажды Ситанатха, поразмыслив, в благоприятный миг совершил первое кормление Гопалы рисом.
В тот день случилась дивная благая игра: по обычаю перед ребёнком положили разные предметы.
Шри Гопаладас не тронул ни одного из них, а коснулся лотосных стоп Шри Гауранги.
Видя это, мой Господь опьянел от любви и сказал: «Этот ребёнок станет венцом праведных.
Стопа брахмана равна стопе Вишну: в стопе брахмана пребывают все святыни».
Так Прабхупада долго толковал и намёками раскрыл истинную суть Гауранги.
Услышав это, преданные ещё больше возрадовались и все вместе начали санкиртану имени.
Плясал Шри Адвайта, плясал Харидас, плясали Шри Ачьютананда и Кришнадас.
Глядя на пляску Кришнамишры, Махапрабху смеялся: Гаура старался, чтобы плясали преданные.
Так день ото дня росло блаженство, и каждый день преданные устраивали праздник.

advaita-prakasha.title: Юный Локанатх из Джессора приходит учиться к Адвайте и с Гададхарой изучает «Бхагавату»
advaita-prakasha.summary: Юный брахман Локанатх Чакраварти, сын ученика Адвайты Падманабхи из Джессора, приходит учиться; по желанию отца он изучает «Бхагавату» с комментарием вместе с Гададхарой Пандитом, а Гаура, слушая их чтение, запоминает стихи и смысл.

verses.text: И вот однажды пришёл юноша-брахман и поклонился стопам Ачарьи.
Шри Адвайта спросил: «Чей ты сын? Зачем пришёл сюда? Расскажи».
Сын брахмана ответил: «Я сын Твоего слуги. Меня зовут Локанатх, по роду я Чакраварти.
Я — сын Падманабхи Чакраварти из Джессора, сосуда Твоей милости».
Сказав: «Узнал!», Господь обнял его. Локанатх сказал: «Ты очистил меня».
Господь сказал: «Сначала расскажи, всё ли благополучно дома». Локанатх ответил: «Всё по Твоей милости».
Господь спросил: «Почему ты пришёл так далеко один?» Локанатх ответил: «Я пришёл учиться».
Господь сказал: «Хорошо, хорошо, оставайся здесь и изучай то, что тебе по сердцу».
Локанатх сказал: «По желанию отца я буду изучать „Шримад-Бхагаватам“ — нектар игр Кришны».
Шри Адвайта сказал: «Твой отец исполнен преданности и всегда опьянён, вкушая сладость „Бхагаваты“».
Затем Локанатх вместе со Шриманом Гададхарой Пандитом изучал «Шри Бхагаватам» с комментарием.
Слушая их чтение, Гаурачандра с великой радостью запомнил наизусть стихи и их смысл.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Sri Advaita Veda-panchanana was teaching His students the Vedas and philosophy.
At that time Sri Gauranga came with Gadadhara to the Acharya to study.
Seeing Gaura and Gadadhara, the Lord in ecstasy cried, "Come in, come in!" and laughed merrily.

Acharya Gosani embraced them both, and then all three sat down together.

We have not seen each other for a long time. What have you been studying all this while — tell Me."
Gaura replied: "Listen, teacher Veda-panchanana: I have come to you from Vidyanagara.
I have no wish to read other shastras — I have come here to hear the meaning of the Vedas."

There for two years He studied smriti and astronomy, then went to the pandit Sudarshana.
With him for two years He studied the six systems of philosophy, then went to Vasudeva Sarvabhauma.
With him He studied logic for two years, and now He has come to you to study the Vedas."

The student said: "The universe exists by its own nature." Gaura replied: "How can the transient be eternal?"
The student said: "The atoms are eternal." Gaura replied: "Inert matter never has activity.
And to ascribe agency to the five (elements) is mere fancy: the sages speak of one Ishvara, consciousness and bliss.
Without a cause the arising of an effect is impossible; the doer is surely He in whom all power resides."

The thing is right in front of you, and you cannot recognize it. Seeing your ignorance, I am very sad."
"Well said!" cried my Lord, roared, and taking Krishnadasa in His arms danced a long time.
Then Mahaprabhu took Krishnadasa in His arms and joyfully gave him the name Krishna Mishra.
From then on Gaura studied the Vedas with great diligence, and the Acharya taught Him most attentively.
Hear one day's wondrous account of Sita, the Mother of the world, whose life was given to Gaura.
Gauranga's favourite delicacy was the champa banana; to treat Gaura, she hid some away.
Mother went to bathe in the Ganga; finding the house empty, Krishna Mishra began to look for something to eat.

"Mother wants to treat Gaura with the bananas; if I eat them, it will be an offence.
But if, after offering them, I eat them as Gauranga's prasada, there will be no fault."
First uttering the great mantra, the pranava, he offered them, saying: "Gauraya namah."
Regarding the bananas as maha-prasada, he touched them to his head and joyfully ate them.
Mother Sita, having bathed in the Ganga, returned home thinking to offer the bananas to Gaura.
Where she had hidden the bananas they were not to be found; thinking her sons had eaten them, she was saddened.

Sri Achyuta replied: "Mother, you know everything: you know my behaviour and my thoughts.
Out of childish mischief I once drank the milk prepared for Gaura's service, and after your punishment I learned my lesson."
What can insignificant I say of the glory of Achyuta, whose soul is non-different from Sri Krishna Chaitanya?
Absorbed in Gaura, he drank the milk meant for Gaura's service, and Achyuta's mother gave him a slap —
and the mark of that slap appeared on Gaura's body! Seeing this, all the people were amazed.
The eternally perfect devotees of Bhagavan and devotion itself — these two have inconceivable power.
Spiritual devotion and the spiritual devotees are non-different in soul from Krishna — so it is written in the shastras.

The Lord said: "Instead of 'Gauraya' you should have said 'Krishnaya.'" The child replied: "The name of Krishna is contained in Gaura."
The Lord was amazed at his words and, overwhelmed with love, kissed the child's face.
Hearing her son's conclusion, Sita was amazed and thought: "Blessed, blessed is my son!"
Then all were called to the meal. Gaura said: "I have already eaten."
The Lord asked: "When did You eat?" Gaura replied: "Someone fed Me bananas while I was asleep."
Having said this, He belched — and, smelling the bananas, all were amazed.
Sri Advaita thought: "Krishna is subject to His devotees: He has surely tasted the bananas offered by Krishna Mishra.
How great is My good fortune to have such a son: by his deeds the world will be purified."
As soon as He thought this, the Lord's heart melted with love, and tears flowed ceaselessly from both His eyes.
Hearing this truth, Sita was lost in love and thought: "There is no limit to my son's good fortune.
I am truly fortunate to have borne a jewel: from my womb a pure devotee of Krishna has appeared."

Sri Advaita asked: "Whose son are you? Why have you come here? Tell Me."
The brahmana's son replied: "I am the son of Your servant. My name is Lokanatha, of the Chakravarti family.
I am the son of Padmanabha Chakravarti of Jessore, a vessel of Your mercy."
Saying, "I know him!", the Lord embraced him. Lokanatha said: "You have purified me."
The Lord said: "First tell Me whether all is well at home." Lokanatha replied: "All is well by Your mercy."
The Lord asked: "Why have you come so far alone?" Lokanatha replied: "I have come to study."
The Lord said: "Good, good, stay here and study whatever is dear to your heart."
Lokanatha said: "At my father's wish I shall study the Srimad Bhagavatam — the nectar of Krishna's pastimes."
Sri Advaita said: "Your father is full of devotion and is always intoxicated with tasting the sweetness of the Bhagavata."
Then Lokanatha, together with Sriman Gadadhara Pandita, studied the Sri Bhagavatam with a commentary.
Listening to their reading, Gaurachandra with great joy learned the verses and their meanings by heart.
One day Sitanatha, after consideration, at an auspicious moment performed Gopala's first rice-feeding.
On that day a wondrous auspicious pastime took place: according to custom various objects were laid before the child.
Sri Gopaladasa touched none of them, but touched the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga.
Seeing this, my Lord was intoxicated with love and said: "This child will become the crown of the righteous.
The foot of a brahmana is equal to the foot of Vishnu: in the foot of a brahmana all holy places abide."
Thus Prabhupada explained at length and by hints revealed the true nature of Gauranga.
Hearing this, the devotees rejoiced still more and all together began the sankirtana of the Name.
Sri Advaita danced, Haridasa danced, Sri Achyutananda and Krishnadasa danced.
Watching Krishna Mishra dance, Mahaprabhu laughed: Gaura took pains to make the devotees dance.
Thus day by day the bliss grew, and every day the devotees held a festival.
Thus a year of Gaura's passed, and in that time He studied the Vedas and the Bhagavata.
Seeing this, the pandits were amazed, and the Acharya spoke of Gaura's unearthly qualities.
Inconceivable is the glory of Gadadhara Pandita: the Four-faced One cannot find the limit of his qualities.
He acquired a wondrous learning in the Bhagavata; the Lord calls him Krishna's internal potency.
Wonderful is the power of association with Sri Gauranga: Lokanatha became a master of the Bhagavata.
Hearing the meaning of the verses, he always shed tears of love, and all said: "Krishna has shown mercy to Lokanatha."
One day Lokanatha said to the Acharya: "Lord, tell me, how is Krishna to be attained?"
The Lord replied: "Receive the mantra of Krishna: it very soon draws Krishna."
Hearing this, Lokanatha rejoiced and received the mantra from my Lord, standing in the waters of the Ganga.
Inconceivable is the power of the king of Vaishnava mantras: as soon as he received it, he obtained pure loving devotion.
Then Lokanatha, clasping the feet of Sri Advaita, wept in the ecstasy of love and humbly offered many praises.
The Lord said: "Do not weep, calm your mind: very soon you will attain Radha and Krishna."
Having said this, the Lord took Lokanatha by the hand and led him to Mahaprabhu.
The Lord said: "Listen carefully, Nimai: teach Lokanatha the search for truth."
Having said this, He entrusted His beloved disciple to Gaura, and Sri Gauranga accepted Lokanatha as His own.
One day Gora said to the Acharya: "Allow Me to leave — I wish to return home."
The Lord said: "To let you go breaks My heart. But you are free both to appear and to disappear."
Having said this, the Lord sank into the ocean of love, and then, restraining His love, said to all:
"This Nimai is extraordinarily learned in all the shastras — I give Him the title Vidyasagara (Ocean of Learning)."
Hearing this, all cried, "Jaya! Jaya!", and the students said: "Vidyasagara, we regard You as our life."

advaita-prakasha.title: Год учёбы Гауры; Локанатх принимает мантру в водах Ганги и вверен Нимаю
advaita-prakasha.summary: За год Гаура изучает Веды и «Бхагавату»; Гададхара, «внутренняя энергия Кришны», обретает дивную учёность в «Бхагавате», Локанатх становится её знатоком и плачет от любви; он просит наставления, принимает от Адвайты мантру Кришны, стоя в Ганге, и Адвайта вверяет его Нимаю, чтобы тот научил его постижению истины.

verses.text: Так прошёл год Гауры, и за это время Он изучил Веды и «Бхагавату».
Видя это, пандиты изумлялись, а Ачарья говорил о неземных достоинствах Гауры.
Непостижимо величие Гададхары Пандита: Четырёхликий не может найти предела его достоинствам.
Он обрёл дивную учёность в «Бхагавате»; Господь называет его внутренней энергией Кришны.
Удивительна сила общения со Шри Гаурангой: Локанатх стал знатоком «Бхагаваты».
Слушая смысл стихов, он всегда проливал слёзы любви, и все говорили: «Кришна явил милость Локанатху».
Однажды Локанатх сказал Ачарье: «Господи, скажи мне, как обрести Кришну?»
Господь ответил: «Прими мантру Кришны: она очень скоро притягивает Кришну».
Услышав это, Локанатх возрадовался и принял мантру у моего Господа, стоя в водах Ганги.
Непостижима сила царской мантры вайшнавов: едва приняв её, он обрёл чистую любовь-преданность.
Тогда Локанатх, обхватив стопы Шри Адвайты, в экстазе любви плакал и смиренно возносил много хвал.
Господь сказал: «Не плачь, успокой ум: очень скоро ты обретёшь Радху и Кришну».
Сказав так, Господь взял Локанатха за руку и подвёл его к Махапрабху.
Господь сказал: «Послушай внимательно, Нимай: научи Локанатха постижению истины».
Сказав так, Он вверил любимого ученика Гауре, и Шри Гауранга принял Локанатха как своего.

Krishna Mishra replied: "Mother, what is wrong with that? I ate them after offering them to Gaura."
Hearing this, Mother Sita smiled slightly and ran after the child with a stick in her hand.
In fear Krishna Mishra ran to Advaita. Seeing Sita behind him, the best of lords said:
"Do not beat him! First I shall hear how it was." Hearing the Lord's prohibition, Sita stopped.
The Lord asked: "Krishna Mishra, what have you done wrong?" Krishna Mishra answered Him gently:
"Mother kept the bananas to treat Gaura. I ate them after offering them to Gaura — I know of no fault."
The Lord asked: "With what mantra did you offer them?" The child replied: "With the pranava: 'Gauraya namah.'"
The Lord said: "Instead of 'Gauraya' you should have said 'Krishnaya.'" The child replied: "The name of Krishna is contained in Gaura."
The Lord was amazed at his words and, overwhelmed with love, kissed the child's face.
Hearing her son's conclusion, Sita was amazed and thought: "Blessed, blessed is my son!"
Then all were called to the meal. Gaura said: "I have already eaten."
The Lord asked: "When did You eat?" Gaura replied: "Someone fed Me bananas while I was asleep."
Having said this, He belched — and, smelling the bananas, all were amazed.
Sri Advaita thought: "Krishna is subject to His devotees: He has surely tasted the bananas offered by Krishna Mishra.
How great is My good fortune to have such a son: by his deeds the world will be purified."
As soon as He thought this, the Lord's heart melted with love, and tears flowed ceaselessly from both His eyes.
Hearing this truth, Sita was lost in love and thought: "There is no limit to my son's good fortune.
I am truly fortunate to have borne a jewel: from my womb a pure devotee of Krishna has appeared."
And then one day a young brahmana came and bowed at the feet of the Acharya.
Sri Advaita asked: "Whose son are you? Why have you come here? Tell Me."
The brahmana's son replied: "I am the son of Your servant. My name is Lokanatha, of the Chakravarti family.
I am the son of Padmanabha Chakravarti of Jessore, a vessel of Your mercy."
Saying, "I know him!", the Lord embraced him. Lokanatha said: "You have purified me."
The Lord said: "First tell Me whether all is well at home." Lokanatha replied: "All is well by Your mercy."
The Lord asked: "Why have you come so far alone?" Lokanatha replied: "I have come to study."
The Lord said: "Good, good, stay here and study whatever is dear to your heart."
Lokanatha said: "At my father's wish I shall study the Srimad Bhagavatam — the nectar of Krishna's pastimes."
Sri Advaita said: "Your father is full of devotion and is always intoxicated with tasting the sweetness of the Bhagavata."
Then Lokanatha, together with Sriman Gadadhara Pandita, studied the Sri Bhagavatam with a commentary.
Listening to their reading, Gaurachandra with great joy learned the verses and their meanings by heart.
One day Sitanatha, after consideration, at an auspicious moment performed Gopala's first rice-feeding.
On that day a wondrous auspicious pastime took place: according to custom various objects were laid before the child.
Sri Gopaladasa touched none of them, but touched the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga.
Seeing this, my Lord was intoxicated with love and said: "This child will become the crown of the righteous.
The foot of a brahmana is equal to the foot of Vishnu: in the foot of a brahmana all holy places abide."
Thus Prabhupada explained at length and by hints revealed the true nature of Gauranga.
Hearing this, the devotees rejoiced still more and all together began the sankirtana of the Name.
Sri Advaita danced, Haridasa danced, Sri Achyutananda and Krishnadasa danced.
Watching Krishna Mishra dance, Mahaprabhu laughed: Gaura took pains to make the devotees dance.
Thus day by day the bliss grew, and every day the devotees held a festival.
Thus a year of Gaura's passed, and in that time He studied the Vedas and the Bhagavata.
Seeing this, the pandits were amazed, and the Acharya spoke of Gaura's unearthly qualities.
Inconceivable is the glory of Gadadhara Pandita: the Four-faced One cannot find the limit of his qualities.
He acquired a wondrous learning in the Bhagavata; the Lord calls him Krishna's internal potency.
Wonderful is the power of association with Sri Gauranga: Lokanatha became a master of the Bhagavata.
Hearing the meaning of the verses, he always shed tears of love, and all said: "Krishna has shown mercy to Lokanatha."
One day Lokanatha said to the Acharya: "Lord, tell me, how is Krishna to be attained?"
The Lord replied: "Receive the mantra of Krishna: it very soon draws Krishna."
Hearing this, Lokanatha rejoiced and received the mantra from my Lord, standing in the waters of the Ganga.
Inconceivable is the power of the king of Vaishnava mantras: as soon as he received it, he obtained pure loving devotion.
Then Lokanatha, clasping the feet of Sri Advaita, wept in the ecstasy of love and humbly offered many praises.
The Lord said: "Do not weep, calm your mind: very soon you will attain Radha and Krishna."
Having said this, the Lord took Lokanatha by the hand and led him to Mahaprabhu.
The Lord said: "Listen carefully, Nimai: teach Lokanatha the search for truth."
Having said this, He entrusted His beloved disciple to Gaura, and Sri Gauranga accepted Lokanatha as His own.
One day Gora said to the Acharya: "Allow Me to leave — I wish to return home."
The Lord said: "To let you go breaks My heart. But you are free both to appear and to disappear."
Having said this, the Lord sank into the ocean of love, and then, restraining His love, said to all:
"This Nimai is extraordinarily learned in all the shastras — I give Him the title Vidyasagara (Ocean of Learning)."
Hearing this, all cried, "Jaya! Jaya!", and the students said: "Vidyasagara, we regard You as our life."
Mahaprabhu duly honoured everyone and set out for home together with the two (Gadadhara and Lokanatha).
What more can I say of Sri Gauranga's departure? Tears flowed from the Lord and all His family.
Meanwhile in Navadvipa Mother Shachi, without Gora, wandered hither and thither like a cow that has lost its calf.
At that time Gaurachandra returned home; seeing Him, Shachi was like one whose life had returned to an empty body.
Gauranga bowed at His mother's feet, and Shachi, embracing Him round the neck, wept uncontrollably.
Gorachand said: "Mother, do not weep, do not weep. I am hungry — go and cook quickly."
Hearing this, Shachi hurried to cook, while Gaura bathed in the Ganga with the devotees and came back.
Having worshipped Vishnu, He offered the food and then joyfully dined with the devotees.
In the afternoon Mahaprabhu wandered about the town and defeated great pandits in debate.
All said: "Nimai Pandita is the crown of scholars. Such a Vidyasagara has never been heard of anywhere."
Little by little the sun of the fame of Gaura the scholar shone forth, and in that same Navadvipa His wedding took place.
Vallabhacharya, like the royal sage Bhishmaka, honoured and respected among noble brahmanas for his family and character —
his daughter was the chaste Lakshmi, the supreme pleasure potency, full of all virtues, exceedingly beautiful.
My Lord calls her Sri Rukmini. Sri Gaurasundara took her as His wife.
Then Gora opened a school and taught students: each student studied whatever shastra he wished.
Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, came — in intellect like Brihaspati, most skilled in the shastras.
Having him, Mahaprabhu rejoiced boundlessly and taught him grammar and poetics.
One day Sri Achyuta asked Gaurachandra: "How can a face be fittingly compared to the moon?
After all, there is a spot visible on the moon, and its colour is a dull silver, secondary."
Hearing this, Nimai Vidyasagara joyfully and affectionately praised Sri Achyutananda and said:
"The comparison of the face (to the moon) lies in its delightfulness. No one thing can be compared (to another) in every respect."
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said: "Now I understand. But another thought has come to my mind:
Madana-Gopala is Krishna, Bhagavan Himself. With whom am I to compare Him?
I find nothing to liken Him to. Tell me a comparison — dispel my doubt."
Hearing the boy's words, Sri Shachinandana, with wonder in His heart, said: "Listen, dear one:
Sri Krishna is being, consciousness and bliss, full of all potencies. He is the standard of comparison, and there is no comparison for Him.
As other tastes are compared to nectar — is there anything in the world with which to compare nectar?"
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta said: "You know everything. The nectar of the name of Hari is sweeter than nectar itself."
Sri Gauranga asked: "How can I firmly believe that?" Sri Achyuta replied: "A thing is revealed by its power:
the gods who drink nectar, when they drink the nectar of the Name, consider themselves to have fully attained their goal — the shastras are the evidence of this."
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu melted with hidden love and, taking Achyuta on His lap, kissed him on the head.
The most secret pastimes of Sri Chaitanya with His devotees — I have no power to describe even their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

cc.title: Первая встреча с Лакшми, дочерью Валлабхачарьи, у Ганги: «Поклоняйся Мне — Я Сам Всевышний (Махешвара)»; она почитает Его цветами и сандалом, Он отвечает шлокой Шримад-Бхагаватам 10.22.25
cc.summary: Однажды дочь Валлабхачарьи по имени Лакшми, омывшись в Ганге, пришла поклоняться богам. Увидев её, Господь ощутил влечение сердца, а Лакшми обрадовалась, увидев Господа; в обоих пробудилась естественная любовь, и, хотя их тела ещё были сокрыты детством, она стала твёрдой. Под предлогом поклонения богам они открыли свои чувства. Господь сказал: «Поклоняйся Мне — Я Сам Всевышний (Махешвара); почтив Меня, получишь желанное благословение». Лакшми умастила Его сандалом с цветами, надела гирлянду из маллики и поклонилась; приняв её поклонение, Господь улыбнулся и, прочтя шлоку (Шримад-Бхагаватам 10.22.25), принял её чувства. Так оба вернулись домой — кто постигнет глубокие лилы Чайтаньи?

verses.text:
(62) Однажды дочь Валлабхачарьи по имени Лакшми пришла омыться в Ганге и совершить поклонение богам этой вселенной.*
та̄̐ре декхи’ прабхура хаила са̄бхила̄ш̣а мана
её увидев, Господа было к ней привлечённый ум
лакш̣мӣ читте сукха па̄ила прабхура дарш́ана
лакшми в сердце удовлетворение обрела Господа при встрече
(63) Когда Господь увидел Лакшми, Он почувствовал к ней сильное влечение. И Лакшми также ощутила в своём сердце огромное блаженство.
са̄хаджика прӣти ду̐ха̄ра карила удайа
естественная любовь в обоих сделала проявление
ба̄лйа-бха̄ве чханна тану хаила ниш́чайа
в детском чувстве скрытый облик стал несомненно
(64) В них проявилась естественная любовь друг к другу, но детство ещё скрывало её истинный облик.*
ду̐ха̄ декхи’ ду̐ха̄ра читте хаила улла̄са
друг друга при виде их в уме было ликование
дева-пӯджа̄-чхале каила ду̐хе парака̄ш́а
богам поклонения под предлогом было их чувств проявление
(65) Когда они встретились, их сердца охватило ликование. И под предлогом поклонения богам они открыли друг другу свои чувства.
прабху кахе, — ‘а̄ма̄’ пӯджа, а̄ми — махеш́вара
Господь сказал — Мне поклоняйся, Я — Всевышний
а̄ма̄ре пӯджиле па̄бе абхӣпсита вара
Мне поклоняясь обретёшь желаемое благословение
(66) Нимай сказал: «Поклоняйся Мне, ведь Я — Сам Всевышний. Почитая Меня, ты получишь все желанные благословения».
лакш̣мӣ та̄̐ра ан̇ге дила са-пуш̣па чандана
Лакшми Его на тело поместила цветы сандал.пасту
маллика̄ра ма̄ла̄ дийа̄ карила вандана
из цветов маллика гирлянду надев вознесла молитвы
(67) Лакшми преподнесла Ему цветы, умастила Его тело сандаловой пастой, украсила Его цветочной гирляндой и вознесла смиренные молитвы.
прабху та̄̐ра пӯджа̄ па̄н̃а̄ ха̄сите ла̄гила
Господь её поклонение приняв улыбаться стал
ш́лока пад̣и’ та̄̐ра бха̄ва ан̇гӣка̄ра каила
стих привёл её настроение принял
(68) Довольный поклонением Лакшми, Господь с улыбкой на устах произнёс стих из “Шримад-Бхагаватам”, тем самым приняв её чувства.
сан̇калпо видитах̣ са̄дхвйо
желание известно, о целомудренные
бхаватӣна̄м̇ мад-арчанам
всех вас Мне поклоняться
майа̄нумодитах̣ со ’сау
Мной принято то желание
сатйо бхавитум архати
истинным стать достойно
(69) “О целомудренные девы! Я знаю ваше желание — поклоняться Мне. Я принимаю его, и оно исполнится, ибо этого достойно”. (Шримад-Бхагаватам, 10.22.25)*
эи-мата лӣла̄ ду̐хе кари’ гела̄ гхаре
таким образом игры оба совершая вернулись домой
гамбхӣра чаитанйа-лӣла̄ ке буджхите па̄ре
сокровенные Чайтаньи игры кто понять способен
(70) После той игры Лакшми и Нимай разошлись по своим домам. Разве под силу кому-то понять сокровенные игры Шри Чайтаньи?
verses.orig:
তাঁরে দেখি’ প্রভুর হৈল সাভিলাষ মন ৷
লক্ষ্মী চিত্তে সুখ পাইল প্রভুর দর্শন ॥ ৬৩ ॥
সাহজিক প্রীতি দুঁহার করিল উদয় ৷
বাল্যভাবে ছন্ন তনু হইল নিশ্চয় ॥ ৬৪ ॥
দুঁহা দেখি’ দুঁহার চিত্তে হইল উল্লাস ৷
দেবপূজা-ছলে কৈল দুঁহে পরকাশ ॥ ৬৫ ॥
প্রভু কহে, — ‘আমা’ পূজ, আমি — মহেশ্বর ৷
আমারে পূজিলে পাবে অভীপ্সিত বর ॥ ৬৬ ॥
লক্ষ্মী তাঁর অঙ্গে দিল স-পুষ্প চন্দন ৷
মল্লিকার মালা দিয়া করিল বন্দন ॥ ৬৭ ॥
প্রভু তাঁর পূজা পাঞা হাসিতে লাগিল ৷
শ্লোক পড়ি’ তাঁর ভাব অঙ্গীকার কৈল ॥ ৬৮ ॥
সঙ্কল্পো বিদিতঃ সাধ্ব্যো ভবতীনাং মদর্চ্চনম্ ৷
ময়ানুমোদিতঃ সোঽসৌ সত্যো ভবিতুমর্হতি ॥ ৬৯ ॥
এইমত লীলা দুঁহে করি’ গেলা ঘরে ৷
গম্ভীর চৈতন্য-লীলা কে বুঝিতে পারে ॥ ৭০ ॥
notes: Заголовок издания: «Встреча с Лакшмидеви, дочерью Валлабхи». «Анубхашья» к 62–68: Валлабхачарья — житель Навадвипы, царский пандит. «Гаура-ганоддеша-дипика» (44): «Прежде он был великим Джанакой, царём Митхилы, а ныне это Валлабхачарья; его считают и Бхишмакой». На его дочери, Лакшмиприя-деви, Шри Гаурахари женился первым браком. «Гаура-ганоддеша-дипика» (45): Шри Джанаки и Рукмини явились в лиле Чайтаньи как его дочь по имени Лакшми; и ещё стих оттуда же: дочь Валлабхачарьи, Лакшми, нисшедшая вместе с Господом, шла с подругами омыться в небесной реке и там предстала Его взору.

Заголовок издания: «Вечная, природная любовь обоих и их радость». «Амрита-праваха-бхашья»: Лакшми — вечная супруга Господа, а Господь — вечный супруг Лакшми; потому их вечная любовь — са̄хаджика, врождённая, и здесь она предстала сокрытой в детском чувстве. В издании Гаудия Матха — чханна тану, «скрытый облик»; у ВЧД — по чтению чханна табху: «хотя их обоюдное влечение было ещё покрыто детским чувством».

«Анубхашья»: это слова Шри Кришны гопи, которые соблюдали обет Катьяяни, желая обрести Кришну: вернув им одежды, Он увидел их желание. Мад-арчанам — поклонение ради того, чтобы обрести Меня; сан̇калпа — сокровенное желание сердца, которое они от стыдливости не высказали; анумодита — «принято». «Амрита-праваха-бхашья»: «О целомудренные, Я понял смысл вашего поклонения, и это Мне особенно радостно; ваше желание достойно исполниться».

verses_en.text:
(62) One day Vallabhācārya’s daughter, Lakṣmī by name, bathed in the Gaṅgā and came to worship the gods.*
tām̐re dekhi’ prabhura haila sābhilāṣa mana
her seeing the Lord’s became longing mind
lakṣmī citte sukha pāila prabhura darśana
Lakṣmī in her heart joy felt the Lord’s at the sight
(63) When the Lord saw her, His heart was drawn to her; and at the sight of the Lord, Lakṣmī felt joy within.
sāhajika prīti dum̐hāra karila udaya
natural love of both made arising
bālya-bhāve channa tanu haila niścaya
in the childhood mood hidden the form became certainly
(64) A natural love awoke in them both, though the mood of childhood still veiled its true form.*
dum̐hā dekhi’ dum̐hāra citte haila ullāsa
each other seeing of both in the hearts arose delight
deva-pūjā-chale kaila dum̐he parakāśa
of worshipping the gods on the pretext did both revealing
(65) Seeing each other, both rejoiced at heart, and on the pretext of worshipping the gods they let their feelings show.
prabhu kahe, — ‘āmā’ pūja, āmi — maheśvara
the Lord says — Me worship, I — the Supreme Lord
āmāre pūjile pābe abhīpsita vara
Me worshipping you will get the desired boon
(66) The Lord said, “Worship Me, for I am Maheśvara, the Supreme Lord. If you worship Me, you will receive the boon you desire.”
lakṣmī tām̐ra aṅge dila sa-puṣpa candana
Lakṣmī His on the body placed with flowers sandal paste
mallikāra mālā diyā karila vandana
of mallikā a garland giving she made obeisance
(67) Lakṣmī placed sandal paste and flowers on His body, offered Him a garland of mallikā jasmine, and bowed to Him.
prabhu tām̐ra pūjā pāñā hāsite lāgila
the Lord her worship receiving to smile began
śloka paḍi’ tām̐ra bhāva aṅgīkāra kaila
a verse reciting her feeling He accepted
(68) Receiving her worship, the Lord began to smile, and by reciting a verse He accepted the sentiment of her heart.
saṅkalpo viditaḥ sādhvyo
the resolve is known O chaste ones
bhavatīnāṁ mad-arcanam
your worship of Me
mayānumoditaḥ so ’sau
by Me approved that very
satyo bhavitum arhati
true to become deserves
(69) “O chaste ones, I know your resolve to worship Me. I accept it, and it deserves to come true.” (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, 10.22.25)*
ei-mata līlā dum̐he kari’ gelā ghare
in this way pastime the two having played went home
gambhīra caitanya-līlā ke bujhite pāre
deep Caitanya’s pastimes who to understand is able
(70) After this pastime the two of them went home. Who can fathom the deep pastimes of Caitanya?

তাঁরে দেখি’ প্রভুর হৈল সাভিলাষ মন ৷

আমারে পূজিলে পাবে অভীপ্সিত বর ॥ ৬৬ ॥
লক্ষ্মী তাঁর অঙ্গে দিল স-পুষ্প চন্দন ৷
